end.competence: Learners are able to explain the drops of water that appear on cold objects, grass and windows, and to drive or walk carefully in fog.
objectives: Define condensation, saturation and dew point.
State the conditions necessary for condensation.
Describe the forms of condensation near the ground and in the atmosphere.
recall: Humidity is the amount of water vapour in the air.
It is measured with a hygrometer and given in percent.
Warm air can hold more water vapour than cold air.
end.recallNote: Check the homework: drops of water seen early in the morning.
situation: On a hot afternoon in Garoua, Yaya takes a very cold bottle of water out of the refrigerator. After a few minutes, the outside of the bottle is covered with drops of water.
The bottle is not leaking. Yaya wonders where these drops came from.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Yaya does not know where the drops of water on the cold bottle came from.
Where did the drops appear, and when?
They appeared on the outside of the cold bottle a few minutes after it was taken out of the refrigerator.
What can Yaya do to see if the water comes from the air?
He can wipe the bottle dry and watch: new drops form again, because the water comes from the air.
end.justification: This lesson will help us to understand how the invisible water vapour of the air becomes dew, fog, mist and clouds.

qa.q: The water vapour in the air touched the cold bottle and became liquid water. What is this change called?
qa.a: This change from water vapour (gas) to liquid water is called condensation. It is the opposite of evaporation.

qa.q: Why did the drops form only on the cold bottle?
qa.a: The air touching the bottle was cooled. Cool air cannot hold as much water vapour as warm air, so the extra vapour became liquid.

qa.q: At what point does air become full of water vapour and start to condense?
qa.a: When air holds all the water vapour it can, it is saturated. The temperature at which condensation begins is the dew point.

sum.title: I. Meaning of Condensation
defs: Condensation is the change of water vapour (a gas) into liquid water or ice.
The dew point is the temperature at which the air becomes saturated and condensation begins.
items: Conditions for Condensation
– The air must be saturated with water vapour.
– The air must be cooled to its dew point.
– There must be tiny particles (dust, salt, smoke) on which water can condense.

qa.q: Look at the diagram. What is the difference between fog and mist?
qa.a: Both are tiny water droplets near the ground. In fog, we cannot see beyond 1 km; in mist, we can see beyond 1 km.

qa.q: On a clear, calm night in the dry season, the ground cools quickly. What forms on the grass in the morning?
qa.a: Dew forms: drops of water on the grass. If the dew point is below 0°C, ice crystals called frost form instead.

qa.title: Question 3
qa.q: Look at the diagram. Which cloud brings the heavy thunderstorms of Garoua in the rainy season?
qa.a: The cumulonimbus, a tall, dark storm cloud, brings heavy rain, thunder and lightning.

sum.title: II. Forms of Condensation
sum.intro: Condensation takes place near the ground and high in the atmosphere. Its main forms are the following:
items: A. Dew and Frost
Dew is drops of water on cool surfaces after a clear, calm night. Frost is ice crystals formed when the dew point is below 0°C.
condensation_forms.png
B. Fog and Mist
Fog is a cloud at ground level, with visibility below 1 km. Mist is a thin fog, with visibility above 1 km.
C. Clouds
A cloud is a mass of tiny water droplets or ice crystals formed when rising air cools to its dew point.
D. Types of Clouds
The main clouds are cirrus (high, feathery), stratus (low, grey layer), cumulus (white, puffy) and cumulonimbus (tall storm cloud).
cloud_types.png

evaluation: The dew point is the temperature at which the air becomes saturated and condensation begins.
Why does dew form after clear, calm nights?
Without clouds, the ground loses heat quickly and cools the air above it to its dew point.
Why is fog dangerous for drivers?
Fog reduces visibility to less than 1 km, so drivers cannot see far ahead.
remediation: The change of water vapour into liquid water is ______.
Air that holds all the water vapour it can is ______.
The temperature at which condensation begins is the ______ point.
Drops of water on grass in the morning are called ______.
A cloud at ground level with visibility below 1 km is ______.
The tall storm cloud is the ______.
end.remediationAnswers: 1. condensation 2. saturated 3. dew 4. dew 5. fog 6. cumulonimbus
end.homework: During the next rain, put an empty tin with straight sides in an open place. After the rain, measure the depth of water in it with a ruler, in millimetres.
teacherNote: The syllabus notions also list drizzle and hail: they are forms of precipitation and are treated in Lesson 35.
Visibility limit between fog and mist (1 km) follows the WMO definition.
